// Every spelling of a silenced type check at an MCP API call site, so the
// sweep in test/unit/manifest.test.ts is proved in the direction that finds
// them rather than only against a source file carrying none.
//
// The name ends in .ts.txt so no walk collecting .ts reaches it and
// tsconfig.test.json's exclude keeps tsc off it, exactly as
// confirmDestructive-call-site.ts.txt and unresolvable-key-call-site.ts.txt
// are handled. sweepMcpCallSites parses it because it passes ScriptKind.TS
// explicitly. Nothing here is meant to type-check or to run.
//
// Twelve call sites. Ten carry a silenced type check: four spellings the first
// reviewer wrote against the two-spelling text sweep, two the second reviewer
// wrote against its widened pattern, and four nobody had tried. Two carry
// none, and they are what stops a sweep passing this fixture by reporting
// every node it meets.

import * as vscode from "vscode";

declare const MCP_PROVIDER_ID: string;
declare const provider: vscode.McpServerDefinitionProvider;
declare const plan: { label: string; command: string; args: string[] };

// 1. A cast to a named type on the provider argument, on the call's own line.
//    The first reviewer's spelling; the retired two-spelling pattern missed it.
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, provider as Spelling1);

// 2. A cast on the vscode.lm object itself, so the method is reached through a
//    type the installed declarations do not carry.
(vscode.lm as Spelling2).registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, provider);

// 3. A cast on the constructed definition, wrapping the whole construction.
//    The assertion's span holds the call site rather than sitting inside it.
const three = new vscode.McpStdioServerDefinition(plan.label, plan.command, plan.args) as Spelling3;

// 4. A cast on the argument to a type spelled out rather than to a name in
//    scope, which is the shape a developer reaches for first.
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, provider as Spelling4);

// 5. TypeScript's angle-bracket assertion, written on the registration call's
//    own line. The second reviewer's first spelling, and the widened pattern
//    saw no `as` in it at all.
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, <Spelling5>{
	onDidChangeMcpServerDefinitions: undefined,
	provideMcpServerDefinitions: () => [],
});

// 6. A cast on the closing line of the multi-line argument literal. The second
//    reviewer's second spelling, and the one a developer reaches for when the
//    provider object will not type-check.
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, {
	onDidChangeMcpServerDefinitions: undefined,
	provideMcpServerDefinitions: () => [],
} as Spelling6);

// 7. A double assertion through unknown, on a continuation line of a
//    multi-line construction. Neither end of it is on the line the call opens.
const seven = new vscode.McpStdioServerDefinition(
	plan.label,
	plan.command,
	plan.args as unknown as Spelling7,
);

// 8. A non-null assertion on the receiver, which silences the checker about
//    the API object rather than about an argument.
vscode.lm!.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, provider);

// 9. A line directive on the line above a multi-line call, where the retired
//    sweep looked only at lines carrying an API name.
// @ts-expect-error
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(
	MCP_PROVIDER_ID,
	provider,
);

// 10. A line directive inside the span of a multi-line construction.
const ten = new vscode.McpStdioServerDefinition(
	plan.label,
	// @ts-ignore
	plan.command,
	plan.args,
);

// 11. Clean. No assertion, no directive, and the sweep must stay silent about
//     it or the guard above would fail on honest source.
vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider(MCP_PROVIDER_ID, {
	onDidChangeMcpServerDefinitions: undefined,
	provideMcpServerDefinitions: () => [],
});

// 12. A const assertion, which narrows a literal's inferred type and cannot
//     make a call compile against declarations that do not carry it. The sweep
//     must stay silent about this one too.
const twelve = new vscode.McpStdioServerDefinition(plan.label, plan.command, ["--json"] as const);
